cards.explanation: The answer is priests. Numbers 3:3 calls Aaron's sons "…the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests." Anointed and ordained, friends, so this wasn't a side gig anybody picked up on a slow week. It was the job they were set apart for.

The answer is offering unauthorized fire. Numbers 3:4 says Nadab and Abihu "…died in the presence of the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai." I think this one hurts, friends. The same verse adds that they had no sons, so only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during Aaron's lifetime.

The answer is False. Numbers 3:4 says Nadab and Abihu "…had no sons…" That's why only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while their father Aaron was alive. No sons, friends, so no stand-ins from that line.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Moses to present the tribe of Levi to Aaron "…to assist him." (Numbers 3:6). Helpers, friends, not heirs. Aaron keeps the priesthood, and the Levites come alongside him.

The answer is the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting. Numbers 3:8 says the Levites "…shall take care of all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting…" Not some of them, friends, all of them. That's a lot to be trusted with, and I get nervous just thinking about the inventory.

The answer is False, and the text is plain about it. Numbers 3:10 says Aaron and his sons carry out the duties of the priesthood, "but any outsider who approaches the tabernacle must be put to death." The tabernacle wasn't open for anybody to wander up to, friends.

The answer is firstborn. The LORD says, "…I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel in place of every firstborn Israelite from the womb." (Numbers 3:12). The Levites stand in for the firstborn, friends. That's the whole idea behind this chapter.

The answer is that He struck down every firstborn there. The LORD says, "On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself all the firstborn in Israel…" (Numbers 3:13). Both things happen on the same day, friends. It's a serious memory, and He is the one pointing back to it.

The answer is True. The LORD says He consecrated all the firstborn in Israel, "…both man and beast." (Numbers 3:13). So the animals count too, friends, along with the people. Then He adds, "They are Mine; I am the LORD."

The answer is every male a month old or more. The LORD says, "You are to count every male a month old or more." (Numbers 3:15). That reaches all the way down to the babies, friends. It's a much wider count than only the grown men.

The answer is performing the duties of the sanctuary. The sanctuary was the family business for Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons, and they camped on the sunrise side, right in front of the Tent of Meeting. I hope somebody packed sunglasses. Numbers 3:38 says their work was a service "…on behalf of the Israelites…" so it was never just for themselves, friends. The same verse has a heavy line about outsiders who approached, and I think that one is serious, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is True. The swap covers the animals too, friends, not just the people. In Numbers 3:41 the LORD says to take "…the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites." It's like swapping out a whole cookie tray, not just the front row. Nothing gets left off the tray.

The answer is more firstborn than Levites. The firstborn males came to 22,273, and the Levites were 22,000 (Numbers 3:43, 39). So the firstborn outnumber the Levites, friends. There's a gap, and the LORD gives Moses a plan for it.

The answer is five shekels. The LORD says, "…you are to collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs." (Numbers 3:47). Same price for each one, friends, no haggling, and He even names which shekel to use. If only every bill came that clear.

The answer is Aaron and his sons. The LORD says, "Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the excess among the Israelites." (Numbers 3:48). Aaron is the priest, and the money goes to him and his sons. Moses collects the money, friends, but he isn't the one who keeps it. Numbers 3:51 says he gave it to Aaron and his sons "…in obedience to the word of the LORD…" I was a 25 cent stamper, so if 1,365 shekels went through my mustache, I'd need to sit down. Moses just hands it over.

The answer is False. Moses collected the redemption money "…from those in excess of the number redeemed by the Levites." (Numbers 3:49). That's the 273 extra firstborn, friends, not all 22,273. The Levites already covered the rest.
